name: Russia-Ukraine War (2022)
description: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24 2022, triggering broad Western sanctions on Russia and a scramble by European countries to replace Russian energy imports.
documented_outcome: Germany, previously roughly half-dependent on Russian pipeline gas, sharply diversified its energy sourcing over the following year - building new LNG import terminals and increasing purchases from Norway, the US, and Qatar - and cut Russian gas imports to near zero by 2023. European wholesale energy prices spiked sharply through 2022 before easing in 2023 as new supply routes came online.

name: US-China Trade War (2018)
description: The US imposed the first round of tariffs on Chinese goods in July 2018, with China retaliating in kind; both sides escalated tariffs over the following two years.
documented_outcome: Many manufacturers began shifting portions of supply chains out of China toward Vietnam, South Korea, and other Asian economies (a trend often called 'China+1'), though bilateral US-China trade volumes remained large overall. Third countries with manufacturing capacity, including South Korea and Japan, saw measurable shifts in trade patterns as firms diversified sourcing.

name: US-Iran Tensions / Soleimani Strike (2020)
description: A US airstrike killed Iranian general Qasem Soleimani on January 3 2020, sharply escalating US-Iran tensions.
documented_outcome: Global oil prices spiked briefly on the news. Iran launched missile strikes on US bases in Iraq days later, but no broader war resulted. Oil markets saw short-term volatility that eased within a few weeks as the immediate crisis did not escalate further.
